_what: A printed position -> {role, spot?, alignment?}. The reading behind the `position` family.
_ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-09. THREE PARTS. (1) EXPAND THE ABBREVIATION -- `LH` is a Left Halfback and `Left Halfback` is the same fact; that is notation and it is safe. (2) A SIDE IS PART OF THE POSITION, NOT NOISE -- Left Halfback and Right Halfback are a real disagreement, and 1920s formations distinguished them. (3) AN UNSTATED SIDE IS SILENCE, NOT A DIFFERENCE -- `Halfback` does not contest `Left Halfback`, it is less specific. A source printing `HB` is not asserting he was not a left halfback; it is not saying. Recording that as a conflict is the same fabrication as `61\"` against `6-1`.
_how_the_silence_works: reading_view.same() compares two dict readings on the fields BOTH carry and treats a field only one of them holds as silence. That mechanism is the draft reading's and there is ONE implementation of it. `spot` and `alignment` are therefore OMITTED when the source does not state them, never filled with a placeholder, because a placeholder turns silence into a claim.
_two_slots_not_one: `spot` holds Left, Right, Middle, Strong, Free and Weak -- one slot, because a middle linebacker and a strong-side linebacker are two different jobs and must contest. `alignment` holds Inside and Outside, which is a separate axis: OLB against LB is silence, OLB against ILB is a difference.
_a_group_is_its_own_role: `DB` reads to Defensive Back and `CB` to Cornerback, and they DO contest. A group name is a different word, not an unstated side, and folding one into a member would be a rule Ryan has not made. It is the largest surviving category and it is reported.
_codes_are_listed_whole: Every code is spelt out rather than parsed by prefix. `LS` is a Long Snapper and `LB` a Linebacker; stripping an `L` would make both of them Left-something.
_refused_is_counted: A token not in this table is UNREADABLE and takes no part in the disagreement test -- it stays as printed and is counted, exactly as an unreadable date is. That covers every multi-position string (`HB-QB`, `RDT-RDE-LDE-LDT`), which state a LIST and are not ruled on here, and codes whose meaning is not settled (`D`, `FW`, `Manager`).

_groups_are_declared_from_the_data._ruled: Ryan, 2026-09-09: a GROUP NAME IS SILENCE ABOUT WHICH MEMBER. `DB` does not contest `CB`. A source saying 'defensive back' is not asserting he was not a cornerback; it is being less specific, exactly as Halfback is less specific than Left Halfback.
_groups_are_declared_from_the_data._how_it_works: the group code reads to {unit} ALONE and states no role. A member reads to {unit, role, spot?}. same() compares the fields both carry, so DB matches CB and CB does not match S.
_groups_are_declared_from_the_data._evidence: co-occurrence on one man-season across every position predicate, measured 2026-09-09 over 51,108 people. NOT football knowledge: the test is whether the archive's own sources put the group code and the member code on the same man in the same year.

DEFENSIVE_BACK._why: every defensive-back code in the archive co-occurs with DB, and DB carries 9,853 claims of its own. No member of this group co-occurs with any other group's code.

LINEBACKER._why: every linebacker code already reads to role `Linebacker` with the spot or alignment in its own field, so `LB` is already silent about which. No change was needed and none was made.

NOT_DECLARED_AND_WHY.OL: THE EVIDENCE IS THIN AND THE RELATIONSHIP IS ARGUABLE. T co-occurs with OL 5 times, G 11, C 4, OT 3, and OG, LT, RT, LG and RG NOT AT ALL. More importantly a 1920s source printing `T` is not stating a side of the ball: two-way players played tackle on both. Putting `T` under Offensive Line would assert something the source does not say. STOPPED, not decided.
NOT_DECLARED_AND_WHY.DL: DE 24, DT 17, NT 2 -- reasonable but not asked for, and DE ALSO co-occurs with E three times. A code that could belong to two groups is exactly the case ruled to stop on.
NOT_DECLARED_AND_WHY.E: LE 16 and RE 14 already fold under `spot`. TE, SE, FL and DE are modern roles and a 1920s `E`; whether one group covers them is arguable. DE would then sit in both E and DL.
NOT_DECLARED_AND_WHY.B: HB 9, FB 17, TB 11, BB 7, WB 6 -- but QB and RB co-occur with `B` NOT ONCE in 51,108 people. A group that excludes the quarterback and the running back is not `Back`, and the data says so rather than my saying so.
